articleBody:
- [ ] Written layout plan — Having a scaled floor plan showing seating, lighting locations, and wall placements prevents costly mid-project changes.
- [ ] Structural framing evaluation — Identifying whether existing partition walls carry roof or ceiling loads determines if engineered beams and permits are mandatory.
- [ ] Electrical circuit assessment — Reviewing existing outlet capacity ensures your entertainment equipment and new recessed lighting will not overload circuits.
- [ ] HVAC vent and duct audit — Checking airflow distribution before removing bulkheads or soffits keeps the living area evenly conditioned during hot Florida summers.
- [ ] Subfloor level and condition check — Inspecting the subfloor for uneven spots ensures hardwood, tile, or luxury vinyl installs flat without squeaks or buckling.
- [ ] Detailed material specification sheet — Selecting paint finishes, baseboard profiles, and light fixtures in advance avoids delays once construction starts.
- [ ] Trade permit responsibility agreement — Specifying in your contract whether you or the builder files for building, electrical, and mechanical permits avoids legal headaches.
- [ ] Dust containment and furniture plan — Planning where to store bulky furniture and isolate return air vents protects your home's air quality during demolition.

How to use this checklist:
